answers.question: My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?
answers.answer:
No, do not double to 80 miles, and do not add doubles. Your body is adapted to around 40 to 50 miles a week from one run a day; jumping to 80 in a single week, five weeks out, is one of the fastest ways to pick up an injury or arrive at the start line flat. Your club mate got to 70 over months or years, not in a week.

What your clubmate runs is not what you need to run. You are on track for sub-3:45 at your current volume: your easy pace has dropped from 10:28/mi to 9:51/mi at the same heart rate, and you held marathon pace comfortably on Wednesday. The job for the next five weeks is quality long runs with marathon-pace work, not raw mileage. We will nudge up to around 44 miles next week and peak near 48, then taper.

new.analysis:
## What this week does
This is your last big build week before we start pulling volume back. The long run is the headline session: 18 miles with 7 marathon-pace miles sandwiched inside, which is the single best predictor of how your race will go. Running marathon pace on tired legs mid-long-run is the specific stress that pays off on Nov 1.

## Why one quality session, not two
Wednesday is a threshold session rather than more marathon pace, because your long run is already carrying marathon-pace work. Two marathon-pace sessions in one week this close to race day would blur the stimulus and leave you flat. The threshold reps at around 8:00/mi lift your ceiling so marathon pace keeps feeling comfortable.

## About Wednesday's drift
On Sep 16 your heart rate drifted +18 bpm from the warm-up into the marathon-pace block. That is partly a short warm-up and partly the pace being honest work. Give yourself 15 to 20 easy minutes before the first fast mile next time, and the drift should settle.

## Looking ahead
After this week we have four weeks left: one more peak week with a longer marathon-pace long run, then three weeks of taper where volume drops but some faster running stays. Trust the pattern you have built, hold your rest days as real rest, and we will arrive at Wexley Lakes sharp.

safetyCallouts.title: Do not double weekly mileage.
safetyCallouts.body: Jumping from 40 to 80 miles in one week, with doubles you have never done, five weeks out from a marathon, carries a high risk of injury or deep fatigue that will not clear before race day. If you want a second opinion on volume from a sports medicine professional or physio, that is reasonable; please do not try this on your own.
